---
title: "Turn triage notes into working event data"
format: html
execute:
  eval: false
manual:
  page: 11
---

The helper notebook turns the current export and the older event records into
the YAML consumed by the website. It also leaves an HTML view of the helper
work so that the row count and current records can be inspected.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm the input snapshot"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
test -s _data/newsletter/Newsletter_Content_Triage.csv
test -f _data/newsletter-events-opportunities.yml
test -f Newsletter_Preproc.qmd
```

Review the export before running this step. The helper may consolidate older
exports into the canonical filename.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Run the triage helper"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
quarto render Newsletter_Preproc.qmd --no-cache --to html --output Newsletter_Preproc.html
```

The R code cleans names, separates section assignments, classifies events and
opportunities, converts Slack emoji shortcodes to Unicode or readable custom
emoji fallbacks, fills required display fields, and writes the current staged
records.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Read the resulting table"}

Open `Newsletter_Preproc.html` and inspect the displayed records. Pay
particular attention to expiration dates, event dates, location, links, and
any remaining colon-delimited emoji names.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="The staged event data exists"}

```{bash}
#| eval: false
test -s _data/newsletter/events-opportunities.yml
rg -n "^(expires|type|title|when|where|preamble|links):" \
  _data/newsletter/events-opportunities.yml | head -40
! rg -n --pcre2 ':[A-Za-z0-9_+\-]+:' \
  _data/newsletter/events-opportunities.yml
```

:::
